name: NeoGrow: Loyalty Points, Rewards Program & Photo Reviews for WooCommerce
author: Pamir

sections.description:
NeoGrow is a free WooCommerce plugin that gives customers loyalty points for buying and for leaving photo reviews, which they spend as a discount at checkout. Everything runs on your own store — no account, no subscription, nothing metered.

What changes on your store

Activate it and these appear by themselves. Nothing to paste in, no block to place, no shortcode to find:

  • Product pages — a line under the price: “Earn 50 points with this item.”
  • The review form — an Upload Photo button, a review title field, and what a review is worth in points.
  • Published reviews — customer photos in a lightbox, a Helpful button, and a way to report a review.
  • Cart and checkout — a panel where the customer spends points for a discount off the total. The block Cart and Checkout are covered as well as the classic ones.
  • My Account — a balance, what it is worth, and a full points history.
  • The order-received page — how many points that order earned.
  • Your order emails — the same line, added to the emails WooCommerce already sends. NeoGrow sends no email of its own unless you switch review reminders on.

Four of those stay invisible until a customer actually has points, so a brand-new store looks quiet at first. That is correct, not broken — and Marketing > NeoGrow > On your store lists every change, says whether it is live, and will show you each one on your own storefront using a sample balance.

NeoGrow helps a WooCommerce store sell more without cutting its prices.

  • Get the reviews that sell. Customers earn points for writing one, and more for adding a photo.
  • Win the second order. A points balance waiting in the basket is a concrete reason to come back.
  • Stop competing on price. A library of real reviews cannot be copied. A discount can be matched tomorrow morning.
  • Costs nothing at any size. Unlimited reviews, photos and points, with no per-contact pricing.

It does that with the two things that actually move revenue: the reviews that convince a stranger to place a first order, and the loyalty points that bring that customer back for a second one. One plugin owns both, on your own store, for free.

Picture a shopper comparing your product with a cheaper one somewhere else. The cheaper page has no reviews. Yours has forty, several with photographs. Most people pay the difference, because forty strangers with nothing to gain are more persuasive than any product description you could write.

That is the whole idea. Your price can be undercut tomorrow morning. Your reputation cannot be copied at all.

What it does for your revenue

1. It gets you the reviews that do the selling.
Customers will happily photograph what they bought — they just need a reason to bother. NeoGrow pays them in points for a review, and pays more for one with a photo. Published research from Northwestern University’s Spiegel Research Center found a product showing five reviews was 270% more likely to be purchased than the same product showing none, and that the lift was larger on higher-priced products than on cheap ones. Reviews are worth more to you the more you charge.

2. It gets you the second order.
Roughly a quarter of first-time customers ever come back on their own. A points balance waiting in the basket is a concrete reason to return, and the second order is the one that matters: once a customer has ordered twice, the odds of a third rise sharply. Points are shown on the product page before the sale, and spent right in the basket — the customer enters how many to use and the discount comes off the subtotal — because a reward nobody spends buys you nothing.

3. It stops you competing on price.
Discounting takes margin off every order, permanently, and any competitor can match it. A library of real reviews takes effort once per product and cannot be copied. NeoGrow is how you build that library on purpose rather than hoping for it.

4. It costs nothing to run, at any size.
Hosted review and loyalty platforms charge by review requests sent, contacts stored, or minutes of video kept — so a good year raises your bill. NeoGrow is free and unlimited. Ten customers or ten thousand, the price is the same.

More on the research behind this, with sources: Why product reviews matter more than price in WooCommerce.

Why NeoGrow rather than a monthly subscription

Nothing sits between the review and the reward.
Elsewhere this takes two plugins wired together: one collects reviews, the other hands out points and watches for them. That join is fragile, and when it quietly breaks you find out from a customer who was promised points and never got them. NeoGrow does both jobs itself, so there is no join to break.

You keep everything if you stop.
Reviews, photos and every point balance sit in your own database. There is no account to create and no company holding a copy, so there is no month where cancelling a subscription empties your product pages. A hosted platform cannot offer this, because holding the data is what it is.

Growing does not cost you more.
Unlimited reviews, unlimited photo uploads, unlimited points, no per-contact pricing and no licence key. Software running on your own store has nothing to meter.

It gives away what you meant to give away.
Points are earned on the order subtotal, so tax and postage never inflate what you hand out. On a multi-currency store the order converts through the exchange rate that order actually used, so you are not overpaying customers in one country and underpaying them in another. Each of those is pinned by tests — and each is a bill you would otherwise pay quietly for years.

Built for AI-first commerce — coming soon.
Search is shifting toward answer engines that read structured data rather than pages. NeoGrow already owns the review content that matters for this; what turns it into machine-readable Review and AggregateRating markup is NeoSEO, a separate free plugin in development. NeoGrow does not require it and works fully without it — the two simply cover different halves of the same job.

Features

Everything below is in the free plugin, with no limits on reviews, photos, customers or points.

Loyalty points

  • Points for purchases. Set a rate such as 1 point per $1 spent. Points are earned on the order subtotal — never on tax, shipping or fees — and credited when the order is marked Completed.
  • Spent at checkout. A panel in the cart and at checkout where the customer enters how many points to use, and the discount comes off the total live. The block Cart and Checkout are covered as well as the classic ones, with nothing to set up. A “Max discount per order” setting caps how much of any order points can pay for.
  • Shown before the sale. “Earn 50 points with this item” under the price on every product page; the points an order earned on the order-received page and in the order emails WooCommerce already sends; and what a review is worth, on the review form.
  • My Account. The customer’s live balance, what it is worth in money, and their full points history.
  • Expiry. Points last 6 months from the day they are earned, and the oldest are always spent first. Choosing your own window, or switching expiry off, is part of NeoGrow Pro.
  • Correct on multi-currency stores. Points are always calculated against your base currency, so the same basket earns the same points whatever currency the customer paid in, and the discount is shown in the currency they are browsing. WooPayments, CURCY and FOX work with no configuration; other switchers connect through two documented filters. If a switcher is converting prices and NeoGrow cannot read its rate, it tells you rather than calculating quietly with the wrong one.
  • Fast on a busy store. Points live in the plugin’s own database tables, not the general-purpose ones WordPress uses for everything else, and the plugin is fully compatible with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage.

Photo reviews

  • Upload Photo on your theme’s own review form. No replacement form, no separate widget. The size limit your server actually accepts is shown beside the button.
  • A review title field. Reviews read like reviews rather than comments.
  • Points for a review, more for one with a photo. Two settings. Points are credited when you approve the review, and the amount never depends on the rating the customer gave.
  • Photos shown with the review, and opened full size in a lightbox.
  • Helpful votes. Customers mark a review helpful and each one shows how many people found it useful.
  • Report a review. A Report link beside the Helpful button lets a customer flag a review to you. One report per person per review, at most ten a day, so a review cannot be buried by one visitor.
  • A disclosure statement above the form saying customers can earn points for reviewing. Editable, accepts {product_name}, and can be switched off.
  • Moderation where you already work. Reviews are approved from WooCommerce’s own Product Reviews screen, which gains the customer’s photo beside each review and a column of open reports.

Review reminders — off by default

  • An email a set number of days after an order completes, asking the customer to review what they bought. It lists only the products on that order they have not already reviewed, quotes the most a review could earn them, and carries a one-click opt-out.
  • An ordinary WooCommerce email, so its subject, heading and styling are edited under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails alongside every other one.
  • A column on the Orders screen showing whether a reminder went out and when, with a button to send one by hand.
  • Never reaches backwards. The clock starts when you switch it on, so a shop with years of completed orders does not email its whole history. Where WooCommerce core is already sending its own review request, NeoGrow stands down rather than email twice.

Running it

  • Setup wizard. Two minutes from activation to a live programme, ending on a summary of what you set up, in money.
  • Growth dashboard. How many orders need action and how many reviews await approval, each linking to the screen where you deal with them, above the points issued, the points spent and how the photos your customers upload are performing.
  • On your store. A screen listing every change NeoGrow makes to your storefront, whether each one is live right now, and where to change it — with a preview that shows you any of them on your own shop as a customer with a sample balance, without touching your points history. It also reports what might stop a change from showing: a page cache, a currency switcher whose rate cannot be read, a block theme on a different render path, or another plugin that also awards points.
  • Points log. A permanent record of every point movement — earned, spent, expired or adjusted — searchable by the customer’s name, login or email.
  • Manual adjustment. Add or remove points for any customer from Users > Edit User, with a reason recorded in the log, and a points column on the Users screen.
  • Branding. Match the plugin’s primary and success colours to your store.
  • Explainer videos. A play button beside the settings that affect your storefront opens a short clip showing what that setting does, on the screen a customer would see it on.
  • Site Health and admin notices. A check under Tools > Site Health reports whether balances are safe from your page cache, and an admin notice appears if a currency switcher is converting prices NeoGrow cannot read. NeoGrow also appears in WooCommerce’s own task list.

Privacy and developers

  • Your data stays yours. Reviews, photos and every balance sit in your own database. No account, no licence key, and nothing leaves your server. Helpful votes and review reports are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools.
  • Three shortcodes, for the rare layout that needs one: [neogrow_points_balance] shows the customer’s balance with its label (attributes label and class), [neogrow_points] shows the bare figure, and [neogrow_cart_redemption] places the redemption panel anywhere else.
  • A documented developer API. The NeoGrow\API\Points class plus hooks and filters for add-ons — rename “points” store-wide from one filter, change what an order earns on, or supply a membership tier.

Documentation

For setup guides, the full list of hooks and filters, and advanced configuration, please visit our official documentation:
NeoGrow documentation

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service during normal operation. Your store data, points ledger and review photos never leave your server.

There is exactly one optional exception:

Deactivation feedback survey (neoplugin.com)

When you deactivate this plugin from the Plugins screen, a short survey asks why. It is entirely optional — “Skip & Deactivate” and “Cancel” send nothing, and selecting “It’s only temporary / troubleshooting” sends nothing.

If you choose to submit the survey, your answer is sent from your server to https://neoplugin.com/neo-deactivation/receiver.php. The request is made by your site, not by your browser.

  • Always sent when you submit: the plugin slug, the plugin version, the reason you selected, and any free-text comment you typed.
  • Only sent if you tick the consent box (unticked by default): your site URL, WordPress version, PHP version, WooCommerce version, whether HPOS is enabled, your active theme name, the folder names of your active plugins, your site locale, and the number of days the plugin has been installed.

No personal data about your customers, no order data and no points data are ever transmitted.

This service is provided by NeoPlugin. Terms: https://neoplugin.com/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://neoplugin.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/neogrow-loyalty directory, or install through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. A notice on the Plugins screen offers the 2-minute Setup Wizard — click Set up NeoGrow.
  3. Set your point values and review rewards. You can run the wizard again any time from Marketing > NeoGrow > Guide.
  4. Navigate to Marketing > NeoGrow to fine-tune your configuration or design.
sections.faq:
I installed it. What actually changed?

Seven things, most of them without any setup at all. Product pages show what each item earns. The review form takes photographs. Published reviews gain those photos, a Helpful button and a report link. The cart and checkout gain a panel for spending points. My Account gains a balance and a full history. The order-received page and your order emails both report the points earned.

Four of those are invisible until somebody has points, which is why a new store can look as though nothing happened. Go to Marketing > NeoGrow > On your store: it lists every change, tells you whether each one is live, and will show you any of them on your own storefront using a sample balance — without writing anything to your points history or letting a customer see it.

Will this actually increase my sales?

It works on the two moments where sales are won or lost. The first is a stranger deciding whether to trust you: research from Northwestern University’s Spiegel Research Center found a product showing five reviews was 270% more likely to be purchased than the same product showing none, and NeoGrow’s job is to get those reviews written by making it worth a customer’s while. The second is whether that customer ever comes back — most do not, unless they have a reason. A points balance waiting in their basket is a reason.

Nothing here is magic, and no plugin can promise a number. What it can do is make the two things that reliably drive revenue happen on purpose rather than by luck.

Won’t giving away points just cost me money?

It is a real cost, and the right question to ask. Three things keep it in your favour. You set the earn rate yourself, so you decide what a point is worth before a single one is issued. Points are calculated on the order subtotal, so you never pay out on tax or postage. And a point only becomes a discount when the customer returns to spend it — which means the cost lands on an order you would not otherwise have had.

How many reviews do I need before it makes a difference?

Fewer than most people expect. The measured conversion benefit largely arrives with the first five reviews on a product, so the urgent gap to close is five rather than five hundred. Confidence keeps climbing after that, so treat five as the starting line.

Won’t a bad review hurt my sales?

Less than a spotless page does. Purchase likelihood peaks around 4.0 to 4.7 stars and falls as a rating nears a perfect 5.0, because shoppers read flawless as edited. NeoGrow rewards a customer for writing a review, never for the rating they give, so you are never in the position of having paid for five stars.

Where is the NeoGrow menu?

NeoGrow lives under Marketing > NeoGrow, alongside WooCommerce’s own marketing tools. If the WooCommerce Marketing menu is disabled on your site, it appears under WooCommerce > NeoGrow instead. Direct links to admin.php?page=neogrow keep working either way.

How does NeoGrow affect my site speed?

NeoGrow is built for scale. Point calculations run against the plugin’s own purpose-built database table rather than the general-purpose ones WordPress uses for everything else, so even with thousands of active customers your checkout stays quick and your server load stays low.

Does NeoGrow work with the Cart and Checkout blocks?

Yes. The redemption panel appears automatically in both the block-based Cart and Checkout and the classic shortcode versions, with no setup needed. Points are applied through the WooCommerce Store API, so the order totals update live without a page reload.

The [neogrow_cart_redemption] shortcode is still available if you want to place the form somewhere else, such as a custom landing page.

Why is the redemption form hidden for some users?

To maintain a clean and high-converting checkout experience, NeoGrow intelligently hides the redemption form if:

  • The user is a Guest (not logged in).
  • The user has a 0 point balance.
    We believe in showing users only the actions they can actually take.

Can I customize the look of the “Redeem” form?

Absolutely. NeoGrow is designed to inherit your theme’s styling for buttons and inputs automatically. If you need more granular control, the form is wrapped in unique CSS classes (.neogrow-redemption-wrap), allowing you to apply custom styles without editing core files.

Points weren’t awarded after a purchase!

Please verify three things:

  • Is the Order Status set to Completed? (Points are issued upon successful completion).
  • Was the user logged in during checkout? (Guest checkouts cannot track point history).
  • Have you saved your settings? Ensure you’ve clicked “Save” in the NeoGrow dashboard at least once to initialize the engine.

Images aren’t uploading to reviews!

Ensure your /wp-content/uploads/ directory is writable. Also, check that the image size doesn’t exceed your server’s maximum upload limit.

Why don’t my dashboard stats update immediately?

To ensure high performance, NeoGrow caches dashboard statistics for one hour. Your live points data is safe; the analytics just take a moment to refresh.

Does NeoGrow count my past reviews or orders?

No. NeoGrow starts tracking from the moment it is activated. It is not retroactive. You can use the “Manual Adjustment” feature to reward long-time customers if needed.

Are Shipping/Taxes included in points?

No. Points are calculated on the order subtotal — the value of the products themselves — so tax, shipping and fees never earn points. Sale prices are already reflected in the subtotal. Coupon discounts are not, so a coupon does not reduce what a customer earns; the neogrow_earn_base_amount filter lets you change that if you would rather it did.

What happens if I refund an order?

Points are not adjusted automatically. Go to Users > Edit User to add or remove points by hand, with a reason recorded in the Points Log. Automatic adjustment on refund and cancellation is available in NeoGrow Pro.

Do points expire?

Yes. Points expire 6 months after they were earned. NeoGrow uses a FIFO (First-In, First-Out) system, so the oldest points are always spent first. Setting your own expiry window, or turning expiry off entirely, is available in NeoGrow Pro, a separate add-on.

Can I reward customers for their birthdays?

NeoGrow is designed to work seamlessly with NeoLite Birthday Bash. While NeoGrow handles the points engine, Birthday Bash automates the ‘Happy Birthday’ rewards, creating a complete retention loop for your store.

What is the notice above the review form?

NeoGrow pays points for reviews, and in several markets an incentivised review programme is expected to say so — the disclosure protects you, the merchant. Since 1.2.5 a short statement sits directly above the review form: “Customers can earn points for leaving a review on this store.” You can edit the wording — or switch the disclosure off with the “Show Review Disclosure” toggle — under Marketing > NeoGrow > Settings, and it only appears while review points are actually switched on — zero both review point options and it disappears.

Is it compatible with my Theme?

Almost certainly, and we test rather than assume. NeoGrow is run against the most-installed WooCommerce themes on WordPress.org before each release, in a real browser on a real store, checking the seven places its output has to appear: the points message on a product page, review titles and customer photos, the photo upload control, the redemption panel on the cart and at checkout, the points-earned notice after an order, and the balance card on My Account.

98 themes tested so far: on 95 of them every one of the seven appears, and on none of them do points, redemption or My Account fail. That includes the themes that override WooCommerce’s own templates — the case most likely to break a plugin — and the block themes.

On the other three, one surface is missing and the rest work: two themes (News Magazine X and SaasLauncher) compose their own product summary, so the points message under the price has nowhere to appear, and one (Create) does not display WooCommerce reviews at all. In each case the theme does not render the WooCommerce output NeoGrow attaches to, and there is nothing for any plugin to hook onto there.

If your theme is not on the list, that means it has not been tested yet, not that it does not work: NeoGrow renders through standard WooCommerce hooks, so any theme that fires them works. Ask and we will add yours.

Still have questions?

Our engineers are here to help! Please open a ticket in the WordPress.org support forum, and we’ll help you get NeoGrow running perfectly on your store.
sections.changelog:
1.2.16

  • Fix: Reviews written on WooCommerce’s own Review Order page – the page its review request email links to – now earn points. WooCommerce writes those reviews without the hooks NeoGrow listens on, and usually without a user, so an auto-approved review from that page was never paid and a held one was paid to nobody. NeoGrow now records the order’s account holder against the review and pays them: at once when the review is approved automatically, or when you approve it.
  • Fix: The points line NeoGrow adds to that email no longer promises the photo rate. The page it links to collects stars and text only, so the line now quotes the text reward, and only on orders that belong to an account – a guest has no balance for points to land in.
  • Developer: New filter neogrow_review_text_points_quote, the per-customer seam for the text-only quote. A review from that page can be paid to a customer whose review carries no user_id; the account holder is in the comment meta _neogrow_review_customer. Extension API 2.1.

1.2.15

  • Fix: The star rating shows again in the review list on themes that keep WooCommerce’s own review markup – Storefront and Twenty Twenty-Five among them. Since 1.2.7 the review layout let the stars shrink to nothing wide, so a review showed its title, text and photo but no stars. The rating was still read out to screen readers and still counted toward the product average. Astra, and other themes that wrap the stars in an element of their own, were never affected.

1.2.14

  • Changed: Review rewards are simpler. A review earns the text reward, or the photo reward when a photo is attached, and nothing else changes what it pays.
  • Removed: A setting and a one-time admin notice added in 1.2.13. Updating deletes the setting’s stored value.
  • Developer: Extension API 2.0, because a review filter added in 1.2.13 was removed.

1.2.13

  • New: A play button against nine settings rows opens a short video showing what that setting does, on the screen a customer would see it on. The clips are served from this plugin’s own page on WordPress.org and fetched only when you click one, so they cost nothing to a store that never opens them and add nothing to the download.
  • New: Review reminders. NeoGrow can email a customer a set number of days after their order completes, asking them to review what they bought. Marketing > NeoGrow > Settings > “Review reminders”, switched off by default — it is the only setting in the plugin that emails your customers, so it is the only one that does not start running on its own. The delay defaults to 14 days, counted from completion.
  • New: The reminder is an ordinary WooCommerce email, so its subject, heading and styling are edited under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails alongside every other one. It lists only the products on that order the customer has not already reviewed, quotes the most a review could earn them, and carries a one-click opt-out that is honoured everywhere — including the manual send button, because it is the same commercial email either way.
  • New: The Orders screen gains a column showing whether a reminder went out and when, with a button to send one by hand. Without it, a merchant fielding “why did I get this email” had nothing to look at but order meta.
  • Changed: Turning reminders on does not reach backwards. The clock starts the moment you enable it, so a shop with three years of completed orders does not email its entire history. Changing “Send after (days)” does apply to orders already waiting, rather than only to orders completed afterwards.
  • Changed: A queued reminder is dropped if the order is refunded, cancelled, failed, trashed or deleted before the day arrives, and everything is re-checked when the job finally runs — an order moved back to processing in the meantime is not asked to review something the shop no longer considers delivered.
  • Changed: Where WooCommerce core is sending its own customer review request, NeoGrow stands down rather than email twice, and the settings screen says so instead of leaving you to work out why a ticked box sends nothing. NeoGrow still adds its points line to core’s email.
  • Developer: New filters neogrow_reminder_review_url (where the email links to; block themes without the classic #tab-reviews anchor should set this), neogrow_core_owns_reminders, and a veto point for targeting rules applied on every path that sends.
  • New: The disclosure statement accepts {product_name}, replaced with the product being reviewed. The statement is one store-wide string shown on every product page, so until now a merchant who wanted it to name the thing being reviewed had no way to say so. Off a product page the tag is removed rather than left showing.
  • Fixed: Reading the settings registry before WooCommerce had started its mailer was fatal, because the reminder field’s help link touches a class extending WC_Email. It now falls back to the email list. Nothing on a normal page load reached this; a WP-CLI command or an add-on filtering fields early did.

1.2.12

  • New: A new screen, Marketing > NeoGrow > On your store, lists every change NeoGrow makes to your storefront — where each one appears, whether it is live right now, and where to change it. It exists because most of what this plugin does is invisible on a new store: four of the seven things it adds only appear once a customer has points, so an empty shop can look as though nothing happened.
  • New: You can browse your own store as a customer sees it. Three settings — a sample balance, your real balance, or a customer with no points at all — so you can see the redemption panel and the My Account card without placing an order or giving yourself points. Nothing is written to your points history, no customer can ever see it, points cannot actually be applied to an order while it is on, and it switches itself off after thirty minutes.
  • New: The dashboard of a store that has not traded yet now explains what is already running instead of showing seven figures all reading zero.
  • Changed: The setup wizard now finishes on the new screen rather than the dashboard, and the notice on the Plugins screen says what has already happened rather than only asking you to configure something.
  • Changed: The Guide tab’s Quick Start no longer lists where each feature appears. That was describing the same things as the new screen, only without your store’s own figures, so it now points there instead — and keeps the two details the new screen does not carry: points for an order arrive when it is marked Completed, and points for a review are credited when you approve it. The “why is the redemption form not visible” answer now tells you to use the preview rather than leaving you to wait for a customer to earn points.
  • New: NeoGrow now appears in WooCommerce’s own task list, which is where WooCommerce asks extensions to put this rather than redirecting you on activation.
  • New: The same screen reports what might stop a change from showing on your particular store — a page cache, a currency switcher whose rate cannot be read, a block theme taking a different render path, or another active plugin that also awards points and therefore keeps a second balance.
  • Developer: New filters neogrow_store_changes and neogrow_competing_points_plugins. Extension API 1.7.

1.2.11

  • Fix: The points log now finds a customer by the name it shows you. The Customer column reads “Marcus Webb (marcus@example.test)”, but searching for Marcus found nothing – the search read the login and the email address, never the name on screen. It now reads all three.
  • Changed: This changelog now carries the four most recent releases, and the full history back to 1.0.0 has moved to changelog.txt, which ships with the plugin. WordPress.org displays at most 5,000 words of a changelog and ours had grown past it, so the oldest release was being cut off the listing.

1.2.10

  • Fix: Searching the points log no longer reads your whole customer table twice for one page of results. On a large store the search could take seconds and got slower as the log grew; it now finds the customers first and reads only their entries, and a search matching nobody stops without touching the log at all.
  • New: The dashboard leads with the two things waiting for you — how many orders need action (processing or on hold) and how many reviews are waiting for approval. The whole card is clickable, taking you straight to the screen where you deal with them. Both are read fresh every time the dashboard loads, not from the hourly cache the other figures use, so the number is never a stale to-do list.
  • New: WooCommerce’s Product Reviews screen now shows the photo a customer attached, beside their review, so you can approve a photo review without opening it. Clicking the thumbnail opens the full picture.
  • Developer: The neogrow_expiry_months docblock said points expire after months of “inactivity”. They expire six months after they were earned — ordering again does not extend points already on the clock. The wording is corrected; the behaviour is unchanged and always was this.

Earlier versions

The full history back to 1.0.0 lives in changelog.txt, which ships with the plugin. It can also be read at https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/browser/neogrow-loyalty/trunk/changelog.txt

  • Stop competing on price. A library of real reviews cannot be copied. A discount can be matched tomorrow morning.
  • Costs nothing at any size. Unlimited reviews, photos and points, with no per-contact pricing.

It does that with the two things that actually move revenue: the reviews that convince a stranger to place a first order, and the loyalty points that bring that customer back for a second one. One plugin owns both, on your own store, for free.

Picture a shopper comparing your product with a cheaper one somewhere else. The cheaper page has no reviews. Yours has forty, several with photographs. Most people pay the difference, because forty strangers with nothing to gain are more persuasive than any product description you could write.

That is the whole idea. Your price can be undercut tomorrow morning. Your reputation cannot be copied at all.

What it does for your revenue

1. It gets you the reviews that do the selling.
Customers will happily photograph what they bought — they just need a reason to bother. NeoGrow pays them in points for a review, and pays more for one with a photo. Published research from Northwestern University’s Spiegel Research Center found a product showing five reviews was 270% more likely to be purchased than the same product showing none, and that the lift was larger on higher-priced products than on cheap ones. Reviews are worth more to you the more you charge.

2. It gets you the second order.
Roughly a quarter of first-time customers ever come back on their own. A points balance waiting in the basket is a concrete reason to return, and the second order is the one that matters: once a customer has ordered twice, the odds of a third rise sharply. Points are shown on the product page before the sale, and spent right in the basket — the customer enters how many to use and the discount comes off the subtotal — because a reward nobody spends buys you nothing.

3. It stops you competing on price.
Discounting takes margin off every order, permanently, and any competitor can match it. A library of real reviews takes effort once per product and cannot be copied. NeoGrow is how you build that library on purpose rather than hoping for it.

4. It costs nothing to run, at any size.
Hosted review and loyalty platforms charge by review requests sent, contacts stored, or minutes of video kept — so a good year raises your bill. NeoGrow is free and unlimited. Ten customers or ten thousand, the price is the same.

More on the research behind this, with sources: Why product reviews matter more than price in WooCommerce.

Why NeoGrow rather than a monthly subscription

Nothing sits between the review and the reward.
Elsewhere this takes two plugins wired together: one collects reviews, the other hands out points and watches for them. That join is fragile, and when it quietly breaks you find out from a customer who was promised points and never got them. NeoGrow does both jobs itself, so there is no join to break.

You keep everything if you stop.
Reviews, photos and every point balance sit in your own database. There is no account to create and no company holding a copy, so there is no month where cancelling a subscription empties your product pages. A hosted platform cannot offer this, because holding the data is what it is.

Growing does not cost you more.
Unlimited reviews, unlimited photo uploads, unlimited points, no per-contact pricing and no licence key. Software running on your own store has nothing to meter.

It gives away what you meant to give away.
Points are earned on the order subtotal, so tax and postage never inflate what you hand out. On a multi-currency store the order converts through the exchange rate that order actually used, so you are not overpaying customers in one country and underpaying them in another. Each of those is pinned by tests — and each is a bill you would otherwise pay quietly for years.

Built for AI-first commerce — coming soon.
Search is shifting toward answer engines that read structured data rather than pages. NeoGrow already owns the review content that matters for this; what turns it into machine-readable Review and AggregateRating markup is NeoSEO, a separate free plugin in development. NeoGrow does not require it and works fully without it — the two simply cover different halves of the same job.

Features

Everything below is in the free plugin, with no limits on reviews, photos, customers or points.

Loyalty points

  • Points for purchases. Set a rate such as 1 point per $1 spent. Points are earned on the order subtotal — never on tax, shipping or fees — and credited when the order is marked Completed.
  • Spent at checkout. A panel in the cart and at checkout where the customer enters how many points to use, and the discount comes off the total live. The block Cart and Checkout are covered as well as the classic ones, with nothing to set up. A “Max discount per order” setting caps how much of any order points can pay for.
  • Shown before the sale. “Earn 50 points with this item” under the price on every product page; the points an order earned on the order-received page and in the order emails WooCommerce already sends; and what a review is worth, on the review form.
  • My Account. The customer’s live balance, what it is worth in money, and their full points history.
  • Expiry. Points last 6 months from the day they are earned, and the oldest are always spent first. Choosing your own window, or switching expiry off, is part of NeoGrow Pro.
  • Correct on multi-currency stores. Points are always calculated against your base currency, so the same basket earns the same points whatever currency the customer paid in, and the discount is shown in the currency they are browsing. WooPayments, CURCY and FOX work with no configuration; other switchers connect through two documented filters. If a switcher is converting prices and NeoGrow cannot read its rate, it tells you rather than calculating quietly with the wrong one.
  • Fast on a busy store. Points live in the plugin’s own database tables, not the general-purpose ones WordPress uses for everything else, and the plugin is fully compatible with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage.

Photo reviews

  • Upload Photo on your theme’s own review form. No replacement form, no separate widget. The size limit your server actually accepts is shown beside the button.
  • A review title field. Reviews read like reviews rather than comments.
  • Points for a review, more for one with a photo. Two settings. Points are credited when you approve the review, and the amount never depends on the rating the customer gave.
  • Photos shown with the review, and opened full size in a lightbox.
  • Helpful votes. Customers mark a review helpful and each one shows how many people found it useful.
  • Report a review. A Report link beside the Helpful button lets a customer flag a review to you. One report per person per review, at most ten a day, so a review cannot be buried by one visitor.
  • A disclosure statement above the form saying customers can earn points for reviewing. Editable, accepts {product_name}, and can be switched off.
  • Moderation where you already work. Reviews are approved from WooCommerce’s own Product Reviews screen, which gains the customer’s photo beside each review and a column of open reports.

Review reminders — off by default

  • An email a set number of days after an order completes, asking the customer to review what they bought. It lists only the products on that order they have not already reviewed, quotes the most a review could earn them, and carries a one-click opt-out.
  • An ordinary WooCommerce email, so its subject, heading and styling are edited under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails alongside every other one.
  • A column on the Orders screen showing whether a reminder went out and when, with a button to send one by hand.
  • Never reaches backwards. The clock starts when you switch it on, so a shop with years of completed orders does not email its whole history. Where WooCommerce core is already sending its own review request, NeoGrow stands down rather than email twice.

Running it

  • Setup wizard. Two minutes from activation to a live programme, ending on a summary of what you set up, in money.
  • Growth dashboard. How many orders need action and how many reviews await approval, each linking to the screen where you deal with them, above the points issued, the points spent and how the photos your customers upload are performing.
  • On your store. A screen listing every change NeoGrow makes to your storefront, whether each one is live right now, and where to change it — with a preview that shows you any of them on your own shop as a customer with a sample balance, without touching your points history. It also reports what might stop a change from showing: a page cache, a currency switcher whose rate cannot be read, a block theme on a different render path, or another plugin that also awards points.
  • Points log. A permanent record of every point movement — earned, spent, expired or adjusted — searchable by the customer’s name, login or email.
  • Manual adjustment. Add or remove points for any customer from Users > Edit User, with a reason recorded in the log, and a points column on the Users screen.
  • Branding. Match the plugin’s primary and success colours to your store.
  • Explainer videos. A play button beside the settings that affect your storefront opens a short clip showing what that setting does, on the screen a customer would see it on.
  • Site Health and admin notices. A check under Tools > Site Health reports whether balances are safe from your page cache, and an admin notice appears if a currency switcher is converting prices NeoGrow cannot read. NeoGrow also appears in WooCommerce’s own task list.

Privacy and developers

  • Your data stays yours. Reviews, photos and every balance sit in your own database. No account, no licence key, and nothing leaves your server. Helpful votes and review reports are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools.
  • Three shortcodes, for the rare layout that needs one: [neogrow_points_balance] shows the customer’s balance with its label (attributes label and class), [neogrow_points] shows the bare figure, and [neogrow_cart_redemption] places the redemption panel anywhere else.
  • A documented developer API. The NeoGrow\API\Points class plus hooks and filters for add-ons — rename “points” store-wide from one filter, change what an order earns on, or supply a membership tier.

Documentation

For setup guides, the full list of hooks and filters, and advanced configuration, please visit our official documentation:
NeoGrow documentation

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service during normal operation. Your store data, points ledger and review photos never leave your server.

There is exactly one optional exception:

Deactivation feedback survey (neoplugin.com)

When you deactivate this plugin from the Plugins screen, a short survey asks why. It is entirely optional — “Skip & Deactivate” and “Cancel” send nothing, and selecting “It’s only temporary / troubleshooting” sends nothing.

If you choose to submit the survey, your answer is sent from your server to https://neoplugin.com/neo-deactivation/receiver.php. The request is made by your site, not by your browser.

  • Always sent when you submit: the plugin slug, the plugin version, the reason you selected, and any free-text comment you typed.
  • Only sent if you tick the consent box (unticked by default): your site URL, WordPress version, PHP version, WooCommerce version, whether HPOS is enabled, your active theme name, the folder names of your active plugins, your site locale, and the number of days the plugin has been installed.

No personal data about your customers, no order data and no points data are ever transmitted.

This service is provided by NeoPlugin. Terms: https://neoplugin.com/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://neoplugin.com/privacy-policy/
